about: TNA Solutions manufactures home textile products (sheet sets, pillow shells, towels, comforters and other top-of-bed items) at a single plant in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, mostly on a B2B basis under customers' brands. About 52% of FY26 revenue came from exports (US, UAE, South Africa and others). It also sells a small B2C range under its own brand Ambra Linens (0.40% of FY26 revenue). It started as an LLP in 2021 and became a company in June 2024.

objects.purpose: Capex: civil construction of new manufacturing unit and purchase of plant and machinery (Dhar, MP)
General corporate purposes (capped at lower of 15% of gross proceeds or Rs 10 crore)

promoters.background: Promoters bring over three decades of combined experience in textile manufacturing, marketing, finance and design. Average acquisition cost is Rs 2.00 per share versus Rs 66-70 price band.

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 83.82% of FY26 revenue (87.42% FY25, 95.84% FY24); top 5 were 61.98% and top customer 23.27%. Exports were 52.03% of FY26 revenue. Sheeting is 50.95% of revenue.

litigation_note: No outstanding criminal, civil, tax or regulatory proceedings disclosed against the company, promoters, directors or KMP. Past delays in statutory filings and statutory dues (GST, ESIC, PF) are disclosed as risk factors.
strengths: Revenue grew from Rs 35.85 crore in FY24 to Rs 104.59 crore in FY26, and PAT rose from Rs 2.69 crore to Rs 9.58 crore.
Diversified home textile range (sheeting, pillows, towels, top-of-bed), though sheeting is still about half of sales.
Export-oriented: about 52% of FY26 revenue came from exports to the US, UAE, South Africa and other markets.
Reported ROCE of 42.84% and RoNW of 32.60% in FY26, with EBITDA margin of 12.12%.
Asset-light model: fabric processing is outsourced while the company retains ownership of the fabric.
Capacity utilisation rose from 70% in FY24 to 75% in FY26; the new unit adds about 68% to installed capacity.
Multi-stage quality control (4-point fabric inspection, AQL final checks) and ERP-based operations.
Experienced promoter-managers; no outstanding litigation disclosed.

risks.title: Operating cash flow negative every year
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was -Rs 8.57 crore (FY24), -Rs 17.26 crore (FY25) and -Rs 18.47 crore (FY26) because growth is tied up in receivables and inventory, despite Rs 9.58 crore of FY26 profit.

risks.title: Very high customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers made up 83.82% of FY26 revenue and top 5 made up 61.98%; the single largest customer was 23.27%. Loss of one buyer would hit sales sharply.

risks.title: Receivables ballooning
risks.detail: Trade receivables rose from Rs 3.92 crore (FY24) to Rs 36.54 crore (FY26); debtor days went from 40 to 128, with export customers 81.40% of receivables.

risks.title: Rising debt and weak debt servicing
risks.detail: Borrowings reached Rs 46.29 crore at Mar-26 (Rs 11.38 crore in FY24); debt-equity is 1.29 and debt service coverage fell to 0.69 from 2.47. Cash was only Rs 0.09 crore.

risks.title: Related-party dealings with group entities
risks.detail: Material FY26 transactions with group entities Avni Impex and Tex Global Inc, including Rs 8.37 crore of related-party sales, Rs 6.32 crore trade advance/purchases and Rs 8.34 crore receivable from them. Avni Impex runs a similar business.

risks.title: Dependence on exports and sheeting
risks.detail: Exports were 52.03% of FY26 revenue, exposing the company to tariffs, currency and trade risks; sheeting alone was 50.95% of revenue.

risks.title: Young company with delayed statutory compliance
risks.detail: Incorporated as a company in June 2024; there were delayed statutory filings (some by hundreds of days) and delayed GST, ESIC and PF payments, with penalties levied.

risks.title: Execution and fund-use risk, low-cost promoter shares
risks.detail: No orders yet placed for the Rs 6.76 crore new plant; Rs 20 crore of proceeds goes to working capital. Promoters hold 50.43% post-issue at Rs 2 average cost versus Rs 66-70 band.

notes: Standalone restated financials (company was an LLP until June 2024; no consolidation). Source tables in lakhs converted to Rs crore. Statements are garbled in extraction and were reconstructed via cross-checks (balance sheet sums, cash flow reconciliation). EBITDA is the RHP-reported figure (excludes other income). Mar-24 reserves not reliably readable (null). Price band Rs 66-70 is printed in the RHP definitions but issue size in rupees is blank ('[]'). nav_per_share left null: the RHP-stated NAV of 119.80 is inconsistent with 1.5 crore pre-issue shares (net worth/share is about 23.96); apparent bonus/share-count change. EPS of 6.41 and 4.73 as reported. Related-party amounts are partly garbled in the source. Peer table taken from RHP; FY24 PAT margin and EPS N.A.
